title: Violations of the Cosmological Principle (Cosmic Dipole)
bottleneck: Radio-galaxy and quasar counts show a dipole anisotropy larger than the CMB dipole predicts, at 3-5 sigma depending on the catalog, suggesting the universe may not be isotropic on the largest scales. It is unknown whether this reflects genuine large-scale structure, subtle survey systematics, or a breakdown of the cosmological principle itself. If the excess dipole is real, it could indicate a giant local void or superhorizon perturbations, each with dramatic implications.
why_it_blocks: The cosmological principle underlies every FLRW-based analysis; its failure would force a rewrite of the standard model from the metric up.
current_state: CatWISE quasar dipole measurements drive the anomaly; independent radio surveys give mixed results, and systematics audits are ongoing. Upcoming all-sky radio surveys with better systematics control should confirm or refute the anomaly within a few years.
